slides.title: 90-161.Z: a path to ANG-wide adoption
slides.subtitle:
Draft r2 · 12 November 2026
For use only after wing PFMs confirm interest. Offices above wing level are not yet identified.
slides.notes: This deck is separate from the wing briefs. It starts only if the interest check shows demand.

slides.title: Why look beyond one wing

cards.label: rule set: every ANG wing follows the same DAFMAN 90-161 duties
set of reviews could serve every wing, instead of each wing repeating them
new licenses expected: standard DoD365 tools only (to confirm)

list: Confirm that wing PFMs want it (interest check).
Find a sponsor above wing level.
Agree on a path with gates, from interest to a formal decision.

slides.title: Path to adoption: each step opens only when its gate passes

phases.name: 1. Interest
phases.what: Ask wing PFMs: current method, access they hold, interest in a pilot
phases.gate: Enough wings say yes to justify a sponsor

phases.name: 2. Sponsor
phases.what: An office above wing level agrees to own it (office not identified)

phases.name: 3. Reviews once
phases.what: Cyber, OPSEC and PA, legal and license, privacy, records at enterprise level
phases.gate: Written answers that cover all wings

phases.name: 4. Multi-wing pilot
phases.what: 2 or 3 wings with less access install from the guide alone
phases.gate: Installs work without the author's help

phases.name: 5. Decision
phases.what: The sponsor decides: optional tool, standard tool, or stop
phases.gate: Support model and funding of time agreed

slides.title: Step 1: what to ask wing PFMs
head: Question
Why it matters
rows: How do you track publications today?
Shows the gap the tool fills
Are you a site owner or site collection admin on your PFM site?
Decides which setup path and fallbacks apply
Which group gives your wing members SharePoint access?
Decides app sharing (AD, Microsoft 365 or SharePoint group)
Would your wing pilot it with test data?
Finds the pilot wings for step 4
How many hours a month could you give to it?
Sizes the support model

slides.title: Who owns it across wings

options.name: A. The author alone
options.what: One PFM builds and supports every wing in addition to their duties.
options.con: Stops when that person moves; cannot support many wings.

options.name: B. Sponsor with owner and backup
options.what: A sponsor names a product owner and a backup; the author leads design.
options.pro: Survives moves; one rule set and one set of reviews.
options.con: Needs a sponsor and time from two people.

options.name: C. Each wing keeps a copy
options.what: Wings copy it once and maintain it themselves.
options.con: Copies drift apart; reviews repeat at every wing.

slides.note: Recommendation by the project; not a decision until a sponsor agrees.

slides.title: Release and change control across wings
head: Control
What it does
rows: Signed releases, checked by two people
No single account can push bad code to every wing
A government-controlled copy of the code
The work survives if a personal account closes
Rule catalog tied to the DAFMAN edition
Every DAFMAN change reaches every wing in one release
Central releases list owned by the sponsor
Every wing's app shows when an update exists
Settings in lists, not code changes
Wings adapt it without making their own copies

slides.title: Risks across wings and what reduces them
Decisions for a sponsor
items: Agree to run the interest check with wing PFMs.
If interest is there: name a sponsor, a product owner and a backup.
Task one set of enterprise reviews.
Approve a 2- or 3-wing pilot from the install guide alone.
